title: Rediscovering forgotten sessions in the Jepsen discography
summary: Callender found twenty unissued RCA sides and recalls two tunes on Lionel Hampton's first Victor date after he left Goodman.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: You were just looking at the Jepsen Discography under the name "Red Callender," and you said yo came across some things you had forgotten about. What did you find there?
Well, I came across at least twenty things that I had forgotten about. A lot of them are on RCA-Victor unissued, and I guess they're waiting until I'm gone before they issue these things.
Why don't you talk to them?

Well, I have to find out who to talk to. Every now and then I find some things...at least someone... I got a note from a guy in Paris that told me about some things that have been reissued in France -- Lionel Hampton's band. I had two tunes on his first record date for Victor when he left Benny Goodman. One thing was "Lost Love" and the other thing was "Bogo(?) Joe." And I hear "Bogo(?) Joe" has been reissued in Europe, but I haven't heard it here -- and I should check it up, because I could use the royalty money.
Maybe you could get some kind of deal to get it released here. It's a shame that we don't get all the breaks they get there, that there's music we don't get to hear.
